issues.description: The template's Farm.singFarmSongVerse method is declared without an Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out), but the problem statement UML and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This prevents students from implementing singFarmSong() by iterating over animals and calling singFarmSongVerse(animal), causing a structural mismatch and a compile-time/design barrier.
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment and declare the parameter so the method signature matches the UML and solution: change the template declaration to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }. Ensure Farm.singFarmSong() iterates over the animals list and calls singFarmSongVerse(animal). Add necessary imports/references to the Animal type if needed.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution repository implements these concrete classes with Space-prefixed names (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat). This creates a naming mismatch for the same conceptual entities and can confuse students mapping the required classes (Seal/Pig/Goat) to the provided solution classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Align names across artifacts. Either rename the solution classes to the expected names (Seal, Pig, Goat) or update the problem statement and template to use the Space-prefixed names. Alternatively, add thin wrapper classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (that delegate to SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat) so the expected identifiers appear consistently for students.
